headline: High risk: Open Interpreter’s default filesystem/clipboard/code-execution surface can amplify Haystack outputs into prompt injection, data leakage, and unsafe actions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Haystack can call MCP servers and REST APIs, so it may emit retrieved content into downstream prompts. Open Interpreter reads clipboard/filesystem and can execute code by default, making it plausible that Haystack output is treated as instructions. The shared bridge is enough for injection risk even without direct proof of a specific parser.
conditions: IF Haystack retrieval results are copied into Open Interpreter prompts or clipboard input
IF Open Interpreter is run with auto-run or equivalent reduced confirmation
IF either agent ingests untrusted retrieved text as instructions
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between agents
Require manual review of Haystack outputs before execution
Keep Open Interpreter confirmation prompts enabled
Restrict Haystack to provenance-tagged sources only
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Haystack has broad network egress and can use MCP/REST, while Open Interpreter can read the entire local filesystem and transmits to configured model providers. If Haystack outputs or retrieved documents include sensitive local data, Open Interpreter can expose them externally through its model-provider calls. The pair creates a realistic exfiltration path in default use.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter is pointed at files containing secrets or regulated data
IF Haystack retrieves or summarizes those files into prompts
IF configured model providers receive the resulting context
mitigations: Do not mount sensitive directories into Open Interpreter
Use a local-only model provider for Open Interpreter
Limit Haystack sources to non-sensitive corpora
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately
requires-engineering: enforce DLP/redaction before model calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress, and Open Interpreter can write the filesystem and modify git state while Haystack can interact via MCP/REST. Their concurrency models do not provide cross-agent locking, only per-process scope for Open Interpreter, so simultaneous writes or repo mutations can conflict in shared workspaces.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same working directory or git repository
IF Haystack-triggered actions and Open Interpreter edits overlap in time
IF no external lock or transaction coordinator is present
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Pause one agent before the other mutates files
Avoid concurrent git operations
Use a file lock around shared resources
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack can generate retrieved facts or summaries, and Open Interpreter can act on them by executing shell commands or modifying files. Because Open Interpreter’s default mode asks for confirmation per code block but can be loosened, Haystack errors can cascade into irreversible actions if treated as authoritative.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter consumes Haystack output as authoritative input
IF the operator approves generated code blocks without independent verification
IF the resulting action changes files, git state, or external systems
mitigations: Verify Haystack outputs against primary sources
Keep Open Interpreter confirmation prompts on
Require a second human review for destructive actions
Limit Open Interpreter to dry-run commands first
requires-engineering: add schema validation for agent handoffs

E_compliance.rationale: Haystack is documented as touching anonymous usage statistics, while Open Interpreter can access anything reachable on the local machine and sends context to configured model providers. That creates a compliance mismatch risk around local data residency and retention, though the profiles do not show a specific regulated class like PHI or EU PII, so medium is the higher justified level.
conditions: IF local machine data includes regulated or contractually restricted content
IF Open Interpreter forwards that content to a third-party model provider
IF retention or residency requirements apply to the same data class
mitigations: Exclude regulated folders from Open Interpreter access
Use providers with acceptable residency terms
Review logging and retention settings
Document the data classes each agent may touch
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing and retention controls
